summary:
The Secure America Act (Pub. L. 119-98, S. 2, enacted June 10, 2026) is a budget reconciliation measure enacted pursuant to title II of S. Con. Res. 33. Its operative mechanism is the direct appropriation of supplemental funds—each drawn "out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated," in addition to amounts otherwise available—for fiscal year 2026 to Department of Homeland Security components, all remaining available until September 30, 2029. The Act contains no substantive amendments to the U.S. Code; it operates entirely through appropriations, referencing existing statutory provisions only to define or condition fund use.

Title I (Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee) appropriates: (1) under section 101, $9,550,000,000 to the CBP Commissioner to hire, pay, train, and equip Border Patrol agents and support personnel for functions "other than immigration enforcement and customs functions," with a restriction (§101(b)) barring use of such funds to recruit, hire, or train processing coordinators after October 31, 2028; (2) under section 102, $7,450,000,000 to the ICE Director for Homeland Security Investigations personnel and operations, of which $108,500,000 is earmarked for child exploitation investigators and forensics analysts, again limited to functions other than immigration/customs enforcement; (3) under section 103, $3,450,000,000 to CBP for nonintrusive inspection equipment, Air and Marine platforms, border surveillance technology, the biometric entry-exit system under section 7208 of the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 (8 U.S.C. 1365b), and drug-interdiction, with a restriction (§103(b)) barring procurement or deployment of surveillance towers not tested and accepted to deliver "autonomous" capabilities (defined in §103(c)); and (4) under section 104, $2,500,000,000 to the DHS Secretary for title I purposes.

Title II (Judiciary Committee) appropriates: (1) under section 201, $13,020,000,000 to CBP for personnel and support to carry out immigration enforcement activities; (2) under section 202, $31,075,000,000 to ICE for nine enumerated purposes, including personnel, removal transportation, information technology, facility and fleet maintenance, expansion of 287(g) agreements under section 287(g) INA (8 U.S.C. 1357(g)), and the Office of the Principal Legal Advisor. Section 202(9) directs not less than $350,000,000 for arrest and detainer operations targeting "covered unlawful aliens" (defined in §202(9)(D) by reference to INA §§ 236(c)(1), 212(a)(2), 237(a)(2), 236/241(a)/287, and 275/276) encountered in jurisdictions that are not "qualified cooperating jurisdictions" (defined via 287(g) agreements or certified compliance with 8 U.S.C. 1373 and 1644), with Indian tribal governments excluded, and a limitation (§202(9)(C)) barring use of such funds to facilitate release except as required by existing law. Section 203 appropriates $2,500,000,000 to the DHS Secretary for title II purposes or paragraphs (3) or (7) of section 100051 of Public Law 119-21.
